title: BoxplotSCI
text: demonstrate various functionalities, use dataset summarySCI::hemoglobin_data. dataset hemoglobin contains hemoglobin values 169 patients 9 different time points. time points column visit_nr coded numeric, time points column visit coded factor. column Arm indicates whether patient Arm Arm B.
code: library(summarySCI) data(hemoglobin_data) hemoglobin <- hemoglobin_data head(hemoglobin) #>    ID   Arm   visit visit_nr  hb #> 1 ID1 Arm B Cycle 9        9 132 #> 2 ID1 Arm B Cycle 8        8 130 #> 3 ID1 Arm B Cycle 7        7 135 #> 4 ID1 Arm B Cycle 6        6 140 #> 5 ID1 Arm B Cycle 5        5 139 #> 6 ID1 Arm B Cycle 4        4 138

title: BoxplotSCI
text: Now let us imagine want order treatment groups reversed.
code: boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin,                    var = hb,                    order = visit_nr,                    group = Arm,                    main = "Boxplots for the two groups",                    legend_position = "topleft") hemoglobin$Arm <- factor(hemoglobin$Arm, levels = c("Arm B",                                                  "Arm A"))  boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin,                    var = hb,                    order = visit_nr,                    group = Arm,                    main = "Reversed treatment order",                    legend_position = "topright")

title: BoxplotSCI
text: names two groups can customized using group_names (legend) group_names_short x-axis. order group_names group_names_short must match order levels(factor(data$group))
code: # back to original order hemoglobin$Arm <- factor(hemoglobin$Arm, levels = c("Arm A",                                                  "Arm B"))  boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin,                    var = hb,                    order = visit_nr,                    group = Arm,                    group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"),                    group_names_short = c("A", "B"),                   main = "Customization of group names",                    legend_position = "topright")

title: BoxplotSCI
text: function can also used one group.
code: boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin[hemoglobin$Arm == "Arm A", ], # Only treatment                   var = hb,                    order = visit_nr,                   main = "Only treatment group")

title: BoxplotSCI
text: function also accept time points given factors. case, user needs make sure factor correctly ordered.  Another equivalent alternative put numeric time points order labels visit.
code: hemoglobin$visit <- factor(hemoglobin$visit,                            levels = c("Cycle 1", "Cycle 2", "Cycle 3",                                        "Cycle 4", "Cycle 5", "Cycle 6",                                        "Cycle 7", "Cycle 8", "Cycle 9")) boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin,                    var = hb,                    order = visit,                    group = Arm,                    group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"),                    group_names_short = c("A", "B"),                   main = "Time points as factor",                    legend_position = "topleft"                   ) boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin,                    var = hb,                    order = visit_nr,                    visit = visit,                   group = Arm,                    group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"),                    group_names_short = c("A", "B"),                   main = "Time points as factor",                    legend_position = "topleft"                   )

title: BoxplotSCI
text: position size legend can easily adapted using arguments legend_position legend_cex, respectively. box can added around legend using legend_bty = "o".
code: boxplotSCI(data = hemoglobin,                    var = hb,                    order = visit_nr,                    group = Arm,                    # short names                   group_names = c("Treatment (Arm A)", "Control (Arm B)"),                    group_names_short = c("A", "B"),                   # Title                   main = "Hemoglobin over time",                    # Legend position                   legend_position = "bottomright",                   # Legend size                   legend_cex = 0.75,                    # Legend box                   legend_bty = "o"                   )

title: BoxplotSCI
text: color size boxes can customized using arguments col boxwex. distance boxes (two groups compared) can adjusted argument shift.

title: summaryByVisit
text: demonstrate various functionalities function, create small dataset. three hypotetical lab-values: LDH, ANC Lymphocytes two categorical variables, grade stage. lab-value measured 10 time points (visits), can divided three visit groups (baseline, treatment follow-). addition, grouping variable called ‘arm’.
code: data<-NULL visit <- c(paste0(rep("Visit ", 10), rbind(c(1:10))),            paste0(rep("Visit ", 10), rbind(c(1:10))),            paste0(rep("Visit ", 10), rbind(c(1:10)))) data <- as.data.frame(cbind( visit, rnorm(30))) data<-as.data.frame(rbind(data, data, data, data, data)) data$visitgroup<- ifelse(data$visit %in% c("Visit 1", "Visit 2"), "Baseline", ifelse(data$visit %in% c("Visit 3", "Visit 4"), "Treatment", "Follow-up")) data$visitgroup<-factor(data$visitgroup, levels = c("Baseline", "Treatment", "Follow-up")) data$LDH<-rnorm(150) data$Lymphocytes<-rnorm(150) data$ANC<-rnorm(150) data$LDH[3]<-NA data$stage <- c(rep("II", 75), rep("I", 75)) data$stage <- ifelse(data$Lymphocytes>1.5, NA, data$stage) data$grade <- c(rep("IV", 50), rep("III", 50), rep("II", 25), rep("I", 25)) data$arm<- c(rep("Arm A", 70), rep("Arm B", 80))

title: summaryTable
text: demonstrate various functionalities function use dataset survival::colon. dataset colon contains data 1858 patients one first successful trials adjuvant chemotherapy colon cancer. simplicity, focus recurrence , two treatment groups, four variable: treatment group (rx), sex (Male), age (age) extent local spread (extent). also add missing values variable extent.
code: library(survival) data(cancer, package="survival")  colon1 <-  colon %>%   group_by(id) %>%   slice(1) %>% # Select the first row within each id group   ungroup() set.seed(123) colon2 <- colon1 %>%   select(rx, sex, age, extent) %>%   filter(rx != "Lev") %>%   mutate(rx = if_else(rx == "Obs", "Control", rx),          extent = if_else(row_number() %in% sample(row_number(), size = round(0.1 * n())), NA, extent)) %>%    rename(Male = sex) %>%    mutate(extent = as.factor(extent)) head(colon2) #> # A tibble: 6 × 4 #>   rx       Male   age extent #>   <chr>   <dbl> <dbl> <fct>  #> 1 Lev+5FU     1    43 3      #> 2 Lev+5FU     1    63 3      #> 3 Control     0    71 2      #> 4 Lev+5FU     0    66 3      #> 5 Control     1    69 3      #> 6 Lev+5FU     0    57 3

title: Creates publication-ready summary tables — summaryTable
text: data data frame tibble containing data summarized. vars Variables include summary table. Need specified quotes, e.g. "age" c("age", "response"). Default variables present data except group. group single column data. Need specified quotes, e.g. "treatment". Summary statistics stratified according variable. Default NULL. labels list containing labels used variables table. NULL, labels automatically taken dataset. label present, variable name taken. stat_cont Summary statistic display continuous variables. Options include "median_IQR", "median_range" (default), "mean_sd", "mean_se" "geomMean_sd". stat_cat Summary statistic display categorical variables. Options include "n_percent" (default) "n", "n_N". continuous_as Type continuous variables. Can either "continuous" (default) "categorical". dichotomous_as Type dichotomous variables. Can either "categorical" (one row per level) "dichotomous" (one row reference level (see argument ref_level), works variable contain missing values, missing = "FALSE" missing_percent = FALSE. continuous_as_categorical subset (vector) continuous vars treated categorical. Default NULL. dichotomous_as_categorical subset (vector) dichotomous vars treated categorical. Default NULL. ref_level Specifies reference level variable display single row. Default first appearing level. syntax follows: ref_level = list(varname ~ "level show"). test Logical. Indicates whether p-values displayed (TRUE) (FALSE). Default FALSE test_cont Test type used calculate p-value continuous variables. used test = TRUE. Options include "t.test", "oneway.test", "kruskal.test" (default two groups), "wilcox.test" (default two groups). test_cat Test type used calculated p-value categorical variables.  used test = TRUE. Options include "fisher.test" (default), "chisq.test", "chisq.test..correct". "fisher.test", exact algorithm runs workspace (FEXACT error, e.g. variables many levels), workspace increased , still insufficient, Monte Carlo p-value (B = 100,000, fixed seed) reported instead; indicated table footnote. NULL, function decides : "chisq.test..correct" categorical variables expected cell counts >=5, "fisher.test" categorical variables expected cell count <5. ci Logical. Indicates whether CI displayed (TRUE) (FALSE). Default FALSE. ci_cont Confidence interval method continuous variables. used ci = TRUE. Options include "t.test" "wilcox.test" (default). ci_cat Confidence interval method categorical variables. Options include "clopper.pearson" (default) "wilson", "wilson..correct", "wald", "wald..correct", "agresti.coull" "jeffreys". NULL, CI displayed. conf_level Numeric. Confidence level. Default 0.95. digits_cont Numeric. Digits summary statistics CI continuous variables. Default 1. digits_cat Numeric. Digits summary statistics CI categorical variables. Default 0. missing Logical. TRUE (default), missing values shown. missing_percent Indicates whether percentages missings shown (TRUE, default) (FALSE) categorical variables. "", options displayed next . missing_text String indicating text shown missing row. Default "Missing". overall Logical. TRUE, additional column total added table. Default FALSE. add_n Logical. TRUE (default), additional column total number non-missing observations variable added. as_flex_table Logical. TRUE (default) gtsummary object converted flextable object. Useful rendering Word. border Logical. TRUE, border drawn around table. available flex_table = TRUE. Default TRUE. word_output Logical. TRUE, table also saved word document. file_path Character string. Specify path Word document containing table. used word_output TRUE. Needs end ".docx".
